oGit 2.2.0 merges pull requests line by line, so changes to different parts of a file no longer conflict.

**Documentation:** https://svnix-solutions.github.io/ogit/. **Upgrading:** replace the binary or image; there are no migrations.

## New

- **Line-level merging.** A file changed on both branches now merges by itself when the changes are on different lines. This applies to merge commits, squash and rebase, and to the merge that Actions tests for a pull request. It runs inside the server, on local and S3 storage, with no git binary.
- **Conflict details.** Pull requests show the conflicting lines of both branches, read-only. `GET /api/v1/repository/<owner>%2F<repo>/pulls/<n>/conflicts` returns the same details.

## Changes in behaviour

- **More pull requests are mergeable.** A clean merge means the lines don't clash, not that the combined code works. Required checks on branch protection test the merged result.
- **What still conflicts:** the same or adjacent lines changed differently, a file changed on one branch and deleted on the other (renames aren't followed), a file added on both with different content, and binary files or files over 1 MiB changed on both branches.
